external_resources: CM4AI project web portal at https://cm4ai.org/, providing project overview, data releases, tools, product documentation, publications, and learning materials.
MassIVE Repository, holding the SEC-MS and AP-MS mass spectrometry data referenced by this release.
Figshare, holding the CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas of iPSCs.
Network Data Exchange (NDEx), via which CM4AI cell maps are shared and which can be visualized in a web browser or accessed via tools such as Cytoscape, HiView, and the Python ndex2 library.

Cell Mapping Toolkit, a series of Python packages implementing the end-to-end cell map construction pipeline, at https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with user documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/.
FAIRSCAPE AI-readiness framework, described with a tutorial and installation instructions at https://fairscape.github.io, available under the MIT License.
Integrative Modeling Platform (IMP) package, available at http://integrativemodeling.org.

d4d_fields.notes: CM4AI consists of three pillars - Data, People, and Ethics - organized into six modules: Data Acquisition, Tools, and Standards (Data); Skills and Workforce Development, and Teaming (People); and Ethics. The project defines AI-Ready biomedical data as fully characterized FAIR data of known provenance that can be ethically and reliably processed by AI applications, whose models and software are available and well-described for validation and re-use, and whose predictions may be fully explained and interpreted to the user as needed; the project's stated criteria are FAIR, Provenanced, Characterized, Explainable, and Ethical. The Standards Module's FAIRSCAPE framework assigns persistent, resolvable, globally unique identifiers using the ARK scheme, with provenance entailments expressed in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology. The CM4AI Tools Module maintains the Multi-Scale Integrated Cell (MuSIC) pipeline, which integrates protein-protein interaction and immunofluorescence image data by node2vec and Human Protein Atlas deep learning embeddings, contrastive co-embedding, and multi-resolution community detection, and which annotates resulting assemblies by alignment to Gene Ontology and Reactome and by a large language model naming approach; this pipeline produces the computed cell maps that the June 2026 release states are not included in this release.
